papers.title: Processing enhances the anti-hepatocellular carcinoma effect of Momordicae Semen via remodeling chemical composition and regulating the Akt/mTOR/STAT3 pathway.
papers.abstract: Momordicae Semen (MS) is a traditional medicinal herb with reported antitumor potential. However, the impact of processing on its chemical composition and the underlying mechanisms against hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remain insufficiently understood. This study aimed to characterize processing-induced chemical changes and elucidate the bioactive constituents and molecular pathways responsible for improved anti-HCC effects. UPLC-QTOF/MS was used to compare chemical differences between crude and processed samples. Network pharmacology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulation
papers.summary: This study shows that processing Momordicae Semen (MS) enhances its anti-liver cancer effects by altering its chemical composition and regulating the Akt/mTOR/STAT3 signaling pathway. Using advanced analytical and computational methods, the authors identified key bioactive compounds and validated their interactions with pathway targets, providing a mechanistic basis for the traditional use of processed MS in cancer treatment.

papers.title: Comparative Structure-Based Analysis of Predicted BZD9L1 Binding Modes Across Human Sirtuins.
papers.abstract: Sirtuins (SIRTs) are NAD+-dependent enzymes implicated in cancer and other diseases, but the high conservation of their catalytic sites complicates the development of isoform-selective inhibitors. BZD9L1 is a benzimidazole-based sirtuin inhibitor with previously reported activity against SIRT1 and SIRT2. However, its potential interactions with other human sirtuin isoforms remain incompletely characterized. Here, we applied a comparative structure-based modelling framework integrating homology modelling, molecular docking, and targeted experimental assessment to investigate plausible binding m
papers.summary: This study uses computational modeling and targeted experiments to predict how the sirtuin inhibitor BZD9L1 binds to different human sirtuin isoforms, revealing potential interactions beyond SIRT1 and SIRT2. The comparative structural analysis provides insights into isoform selectivity that could guide the design of more specific sirtuin inhibitors for cancer therapy.

papers.title: Identification of Natural Flavonoids Targeting PLK-1 as Potential Anti-Metastatic Agents: A Computational Approach.
papers.abstract: This study combines ligand- and structure-based in silico strategies to predict the inhibitory activity of natural flavonoids on the Polo-Like Kinase-1 (PLK-1) enzyme as candidate anticancer agents. This enzyme participates in mitosis and is overexpressed in cancer cells. Furthermore, it has been shown to have important implications for tumor metastasis, and its inhibitors are attractive starting points for drug development. First, classification models are developed using linear discriminant analysis and a multilayer perceptron neural network. Models with accuracy greater than 80%, validated
papers.summary: This study uses computational methods to identify natural flavonoids that may inhibit PLK-1, an enzyme overexpressed in cancer and linked to metastasis. The authors developed classification models with high accuracy to predict inhibitory activity, suggesting these compounds as potential anti-metastatic drug candidates.

papers.title: Molecular Mechanisms of Foreign Body Responses to Neural Electrodes and Surface Biofunctionalization Strategies for Interface Modulation.
papers.abstract: Long-term implantable neural electrodes underpin brain-machine interfaces, deep brain stimulation, epilepsy monitoring, and closed-loop neuromodulation. Following chronic implantation, however, the foreign body response (FBR) at the electrode-tissue interface remains a major constraint on long-term performance, as reflected by increased interfacial impedance, lower signal-to-noise ratios, fewer resolvable units, and higher stimulation thresholds. This deterioration arises from interrelated events that include implantation injury, protein adsorption, blood-brain barrier disruption, complement a
papers.summary: This review examines the molecular mechanisms underlying the foreign body response (FBR) to chronic neural electrodes, which degrades their performance over time, and discusses surface biofunctionalization strategies to modulate the electrode-tissue interface. It highlights key events such as protein adsorption, glial scarring, and inflammation, and evaluates approaches to improve long-term neural interfacing.

papers.title: CdS-Based Photocatalysts for Antimicrobial Applications: From Quantum Dots to Z-Scheme Heterojunctions-Mechanisms, Challenges, and Future Perspectives.
papers.abstract: The chronic overuse of antibiotics has accelerated the emergence of antibiotic-resistant bacteria, creating a global public health crisis as conventional therapies fail against multidrug-resistant pathogens spreading through water and food chains. Cadmium sulfide (CdS) has been established as an important visible-light-driven photocatalyst for antibacterial applications. This brief review systematically examines the structure-property relationships governing CdS-based antibacterial materials, including crystallographic polymorphs (cubic sphalerite and hexagonal wurtzite), morphological diversi
papers.summary: This review summarizes the use of cadmium sulfide (CdS) photocatalysts for antibacterial applications, covering mechanisms, material design strategies (from quantum dots to Z-scheme heterojunctions), and current challenges. It highlights the potential of CdS-based materials as an alternative to conventional antibiotics for combating drug-resistant bacteria.

papers.title: FDA-Approved Drug Repurposing as p53 Mutants Rescue Candidates Using Structure-Based Virtual Screening and Molecular Simulations.
papers.abstract: The restoration of mutant p53 stability is a highly sought-after strategy in targeted cancer therapy. This study presents a structure-based virtual screening and molecular dynamics approach to nominate FDA-approved drugs as candidate stabilizers of mutant p53 for downstream experimental validation. A virtual screening library of FDA-approved compounds was docked against three representative p53 mutants (7DHY, 7DHZ, and 7V97) to evaluate their binding potential. The prioritized candidates demonstrated consistent, multi-conformer binding affinities. Protein-ligand interaction profiling revealed
papers.summary: This study uses structure-based virtual screening and molecular dynamics simulations to identify FDA-approved drugs that could stabilize mutant p53, a key target in cancer therapy. The authors docked a library of approved compounds against three p53 mutants and prioritized candidates with consistent binding affinities and favorable interaction profiles, providing a shortlist for experimental validation.

papers.title: Solvent Interaction Analysis: A New Lens for Protein Structure and Diagnostics.
papers.abstract: Aqueous two-phase systems (ATPSs) provide a versatile, fully aqueous platform for probing solute-water interactions and protein structure. This review first surveys the diversity and phase behavior of biphasic aqueous systems formed by polymers and salts. We describe how phase diagrams characterize ATPS formation and composition and how both polymer chemistry and salt identity, rather than molecular size alone, govern phase separation by modulating the solvent properties of water. Building on a modified binodal model, we show that phase separation and solute partitioning can be understood in t
papers.summary: This review introduces aqueous two-phase systems (ATPSs) as a versatile platform for probing solute-water interactions and protein structure, emphasizing that polymer chemistry and salt identity, rather than molecular size alone, govern phase separation by modulating water's solvent properties. It presents a modified binodal model to explain phase separation and solute partitioning, offering a new lens for protein diagnostics and structural analysis.

papers.title: Identification and functional characterization of a SUZ12 frameshift variant in a Chinese family with Imagawa-Matsumoto syndrome.
papers.abstract: Imagawa-Matsumoto syndrome (IMMAS) is a rare overgrowth disorder caused by heterozygous loss-of-function variants in SUZ12, which encodes a core subunit of the Polycomb Repressive Complex 2 (PRC2). To date, fewer than 20 cases have been reported, and the molecular mechanisms underlying PRC2 dysfunction in IMMAS remain incompletely understood.
papers.summary: This study identifies a novel SUZ12 frameshift variant in a Chinese family with Imagawa-Matsumoto syndrome (IMMAS), a rare overgrowth disorder, and functionally characterizes its impact on PRC2 function. The findings expand the known mutational spectrum of SUZ12 and provide further evidence linking PRC2 dysfunction to the molecular pathogenesis of IMMAS.

papers.title: Molecular Dynamics and Electron Density Topology Reveal Ligand-Specific Interaction Patterns at the Dopamine D2 Receptor.
papers.abstract: The dopamine D2 receptor (D2R) is one of the principal therapeutic targets for the treatment of schizophrenia and other neuropsychiatric disorders. Understanding how ligands with different pharmacological profiles interact with D2R is essential for the rational design of safer and more effective antipsychotic drugs. In this work, Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations combined with Quantum Theory of Atoms in Molecules (QTAIM) analysis were employed to investigate the electronic nature of protein-ligand interactions in D2R embedded in a neuronal membrane environment. Representative agonists (dopam
papers.summary: This study uses molecular dynamics simulations combined with quantum theory of atoms in molecules (QTAIM) analysis to characterize the electronic interaction patterns between the dopamine D2 receptor and ligands with different pharmacological profiles, including agonists and antipsychotics. The findings reveal ligand-specific interaction patterns that could inform the rational design of safer and more effective antipsychotic drugs.

papers.title: Linear Residual Network Modeling for Anti-HIV-1 Activity Prediction and Docking-Validated Design of Biphenyl-DAPY-Based NNRTIs.
papers.abstract: To predict the anti-HIV-1 activity of biphenyl-DAPY-based non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NNRTIs), a quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) analysis was conducted. Using the heuristic method (HM) for descriptor selection, four predictive models were established: support vector regression (SVR), kernel ridge regression, linear mixed-kernel SVR, and Linear Residual Network (LRNet). Rigorous validations, including leave-one-out cross-validation, fivefold cross-validation, and Y-randomization tests, confirmed their reliability. The LRNet model exhibited the best perfo
papers.summary: This study develops QSAR models to predict anti-HIV-1 activity of biphenyl-DAPY-based NNRTIs, with the Linear Residual Network (LRNet) model showing the best performance. The models were validated through cross-validation and Y-randomization, and docking was used to validate the design of new compounds.

papers.title: Trans-interface coupling in the tetrameric enzyme underlies allosteric control in Escherichia coli biosynthetic threonine deaminase.
papers.abstract: Allosteric regulation in biosynthetic L-threonine deaminase (BTD) has long been attributed to effector-induced conformational changes. Here, we identify a trans-interface coupling mechanism that regulates the active site architecture of EcIlvA, the BTD homolog of Escherichia coli. Starting from a low-activity, regulatory-domain-truncated variant (EcIlvA1-335, termed CDL) that retains only the catalytic domain and the native linker region, we combined computational screening with experimental selection and directed evolution to identify a variant (designated HSG) bearing three mutations in the
papers.summary: This study reveals a novel trans-interface coupling mechanism in E. coli threonine deaminase (EcIlvA) that controls active site architecture, challenging the traditional view that allosteric regulation solely depends on effector-induced conformational changes. By combining computational screening with directed evolution, the authors identified a variant with three mutations that modulate enzyme activity, providing new insights into allosteric control in tetrameric enzymes.

papers.title: The crystal structure of the activin B:Fst288 complex and computational insights into the broad antagonistic activity and specificity of follistatin.
papers.abstract: Members of the transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β) family regulate essential biological processes, and their activity is tightly controlled by extracellular antagonists like follistatin 288 (Fst288). While Fst288 potently inhibits several ligands, including activins A and B, GDF8, and GDF11, the structural basis for its interaction with activin B (ActB) has remained largely uncharacterized. This lack of data has limited our understanding of how Fst288 achieves such broad inhibitory activity while maintaining ligand-specific selectivity. In this study, we resolved the crystal structure of the
papers.summary: This study resolves the crystal structure of the activin B:Fst288 complex, revealing how follistatin achieves broad inhibition of TGF-β ligands while maintaining specificity. Computational analyses provide insights into the molecular determinants of Fst288's antagonistic activity, advancing our understanding of extracellular regulation of this important signaling family.

papers.title: Host immune network-guided reverse vaccinology approach for prioritizing candidate antigens in Schistosoma japonicum-associated liver fibrosis.
papers.abstract: Schistosoma japonicum-associated liver fibrosis (SSLF) remains a major cause of long-term morbidity in schistosomiasis, even in post-control or low-transmission settings. While most vaccine development efforts have focused on reducing parasite burden, few approaches have incorporated host pathology related to liver fibrosis. This study developed an in silico strategy that combined host single-cell analysis with reverse vaccinology to guide the exploratory screening of parasite antigens with potential relevance to SSLF. Single-cell transcriptomics of fibrotic and control human liver tissues was
papers.summary: This study presents a computational strategy that integrates host single-cell transcriptomics with reverse vaccinology to prioritize Schistosoma japonicum antigens potentially involved in liver fibrosis. By analyzing fibrotic versus control human liver tissues, the approach identifies parasite antigens that may interact with host immune pathways driving fibrosis, offering a new avenue for vaccine development targeting disease pathology rather than just parasite burden.

papers.title: Viral Nuclease Inhibitors: Small molecule disruptors of the UL12 alkaline nuclease display broad anti-herpes virus activity.
papers.abstract: Herpes simplex virus 1 (HSV-1) UL12 encodes a highly conserved 5' → 3' alkaline exonuclease that is essential for the production of infectious virus. Together with the viral single-stranded DNA-binding/annealing protein ICP8, UL12 functions as a two-component recombinase that mediates recombination-dependent viral DNA replication. Here, we present the crystal structure of the catalytic domain of the HSV alkaline nuclease (UL12), which provides the first view of an α-herpesvirus alkaline nuclease. Using this structure, we optimized a series of small-molecule viral nuclease inhibitors (VNIs) tha
papers.summary: This study presents the first crystal structure of the HSV-1 UL12 alkaline nuclease catalytic domain and uses it to optimize small-molecule inhibitors that disrupt viral nuclease activity. These inhibitors show broad anti-herpesvirus activity, highlighting a potential new antiviral strategy targeting a conserved viral enzyme.

papers.title: Sabinene attenuates inflammation and oxidative stress in CFA-induced arthritis: In vivo and in silico evidence implicating TLR4/NLRP3/NF-κB signaling.
papers.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic immune-mediated disease in which persistent inflammation and oxidative stress contribute to progressive joint damage. This study evaluated the prophylactic effects of sabinene in complete Freund's adjuvant (CFA)-induced arthritis and explored potential molecular associations using integrated in vivo and computational approaches. Rats were allocated to vehicle control, arthritic control, piroxicam, or sabinene groups (15, 30, or 60 mg/kg; n = 6/group); sabinene was administered orally beginning 30 minutes before CFA injection and continued for 28 days. Paw
papers.summary: This study demonstrates that sabinene, a natural monoterpene, reduces inflammation and oxidative stress in a rat model of rheumatoid arthritis, likely by inhibiting TLR4/NLRP3/NF-κB signaling. The findings, supported by in silico analysis, suggest sabinene as a potential therapeutic candidate for RA.

papers.title: An integrated approach: green extraction technique optimization, mechanistic study, and bioactivity profiling of four flavonoids from Epimedium sagittatum.
papers.abstract: In this study, a novel strategy for simultaneous extraction of four key flavonoids (epimedin A, epimedin B, epimedin C, and icariin) from Epimedium sagittatum using deep eutectic solvent-ultrasound assisted extraction (DES-UAE) was developed. Initially, 24 kinds of DESs were produced, a proline-lactic acid system demonstrated optimal extraction efficiency. The ideal parameters were established by single-factor experiments and response surface methodology optimization: water content of 29%, molar ratio of 1 : 1.9, liquid-solid ratio of 32 : 1 mL g-1, ultrasound power of 280 W and extraction tim
papers.summary: This study develops a green extraction method using deep eutectic solvents combined with ultrasound to efficiently extract four bioactive flavonoids from Epimedium sagittatum, optimizing conditions via response surface methodology. It also includes mechanistic insights and bioactivity profiling, offering a sustainable alternative for natural product extraction.

papers.title: In silico, in vitro, and in vivo evaluation of the antiviral potential of glycyrrhizic acid and chitosan nanoparticles against foot and mouth disease virus.
papers.abstract: Foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) considers as one of the extremely infectious diseases with major economic impact on cloven-hoofed animals globally. The causative agent of the disease, Foot and Mouth Disease Virus (FMDV), comprises seven serotypes designated as; O, A, SAT1, SAT2, SAT3, C, and Asia1. Over the past decades, studies have shown that glycyrrhizic acid, the primary bioactive compound of licorice root, and chitosan, as a biodegradable and biocompatible natural polymer derived from crustacean shells, are potent candidates for inhibition of FMDV activity. The current work evaluated the pot
papers.summary: This study evaluates the antiviral potential of glycyrrhizic acid and chitosan nanoparticles against foot-and-mouth disease virus (FMDV) using in silico, in vitro, and in vivo approaches. The findings suggest these compounds may inhibit FMDV activity, offering a potential therapeutic strategy against this economically devastating livestock disease.

papers.title: Structure-based TCR-pMHC binding prediction and generalization to unseen peptides.
papers.abstract: The interaction between T-cell receptors (TCRs) with the peptide-bound major histocompatibility complex (MHC) intricately impacts the functional specificity of T-cell-mediated adaptive immune response. Consequently, implication in immunotherapy has contributed to the ever-growing computational methods for TCR recognition, which have recently attracted structure-based approaches due to advancements in protein structure modeling. Despite access to structural information of the predicted binding interface, graph neural network (GNN)-based TCR-pMHC binding specificity classifiers tend to show poor
papers.summary: This paper presents a structure-based approach for predicting TCR-pMHC binding specificity, leveraging predicted structural information and graph neural networks. The authors address the challenge of generalizing to unseen peptides, which is critical for immunotherapy applications. The work highlights the limitations of current GNN-based classifiers and proposes improvements to enhance predictive performance on novel peptide targets.

papers.title: Glycoconjugate strategy for GLUT-driven curcumin delivery and anticancer activity in breast cancer cells.
papers.abstract: Selective targeting of cancer cells is a critical strategy in anticancer therapy, and the overexpression of glucose transporters (GLUTs) in malignant cells provides an attractive avenue for achieving this selectivity. In this study, we report the synthesis and biological evaluation of glycoconjugate vanadyl complexes as GLUT-directed anticancer agents against breast cancer. A Schiff base ligand (CG) was synthesized through the condensation of curcumin (C) and glucosamine (G), followed by complexation with vanadyl to form [VO(CG)₂]·5H₂O. The synthesized compounds were comprehensively characteri
papers.summary: This study reports the synthesis of a curcumin-glucosamine conjugate complexed with vanadyl, designed to target glucose transporters (GLUTs) overexpressed in breast cancer cells. The glycoconjugate showed selective anticancer activity, suggesting a promising strategy for GLUT-driven drug delivery in cancer therapy.

papers.title: Coiled-Coil Domain Kinking Controls Laminin-332 Cleavage by Elastase.
papers.abstract: Laminins are integral components of basement membranes, where they provide structural support and mediate integrin-dependent cell adhesion. A flexible coiled-coil domain forms the laminin long arm, but ultrastructural insight into this domain is limited, and the function of coiled-coil flexibility remains unclear. Here, we use high-speed atomic force microscopy (HS-AFM) to visualize, in real-time, the digestion of individual laminin-332 molecules by pancreatic elastase and show that coiled-coil kinking directs elastase cleavage to the hinge site, thereby generating the elastase 8 (E8) fragment
papers.summary: This study uses high-speed atomic force microscopy to visualize in real time how pancreatic elastase digests individual laminin-332 molecules, revealing that kinking of the coiled-coil domain directs cleavage to the hinge site and generates the elastase 8 fragment. The findings provide new ultrastructural insight into the flexible laminin long arm and demonstrate that coiled-coil flexibility is functionally important for proteolytic processing.

papers.title: Exploring rare coumarins biosynthesis by Gloeophyllum trabeum: an integrated computational genomics, molecular docking and spectroscopic approach.
papers.abstract: The sustained rise of antibiotics resistance demands the discovery of novel compounds to enhance current treatment efficiency and decrease the spread of resistant pathogens. Gloeophyllum trabeum is a common wood-decaying basidiomycete fungus, however its capability for production of specialised metabolites remains poorly understood. We integrated spectroscopic analysis, computational genomic, and molecular docking to explore isocoumarin biosynthesis of this mushroom. Using plate-based overlay bioassays we showed that G. trabeum is antagonistic against three microbes: Escherichia coli, Saccharo
papers.summary: This study investigates the biosynthesis of rare coumarins in the wood-decaying fungus Gloeophyllum trabeum by integrating genomic analysis, molecular docking, and spectroscopic methods. The authors demonstrate that G. trabeum produces isocoumarins with antimicrobial activity against Escherichia coli and other microbes, highlighting its potential as a source of novel antibiotic compounds.

papers.title: Expression, purification, crystallization and structure solution of glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase from the babesiosis infective agent Babesia bovis.
papers.abstract: Babesia bovis is a species of apicomplexan hemoparasitic protozoa that can be transmitted by ticks, causing a global cattle disease. As it depends mainly on the glycolytic pathway for energy production and life cycle maintenance, glycolytic enzymes are possible targets for drug development against Babesia. Glyceraldehyde-3-Phosphate Dehydrogenase (GAPDH) has been one of such targets, against several parasitic organisms. It performs the reversible oxidative phosphorylation of glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate to 1,3-bisphospho-D-glycerate in the presence of nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide. The proto
papers.summary: This study reports the expression, purification, crystallization, and structure solution of glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase (GAPDH) from Babesia bovis, a tick-borne parasite causing cattle babesiosis. The structural characterization of this glycolytic enzyme provides a foundation for structure-based drug design against this pathogen.

papers.title: Discovery of Novel Druggable Binding Pockets on SARS-CoV-2 PLpro via Fragment Screening and Insights for Structure-Based Inhibitor Design.
papers.abstract: Coronaviruses are a large family of viruses capable of causing severe respiratory diseases, with recent outbreaks posing major threats to global public health. The SARS-CoV-2 papain-like protease (PLpro) is an essential viral enzyme involved in viral replication and host immune evasion, making it an attractive target for antiviral drug development. However, no PLpro-targeted drugs have yet been approved. Here, we employed a fragment-based drug discovery (FBDD) strategy combined with crystallographic screening and identified 23 fragment compounds with well-defined electron density. These fragme
papers.summary: This study used fragment-based drug discovery and crystallographic screening to identify 23 fragment compounds binding to SARS-CoV-2 PLpro, revealing novel druggable binding pockets. The findings provide new structural insights and a foundation for designing PLpro-targeted antiviral inhibitors.

papers.title: Improving Activity and Stability of Candida boidinii Formate Dehydrogenase Through Rational Active Site Engineering.
papers.abstract: Formate dehydrogenases represent a highly attractive tool for nicotinamide cofactor regeneration to drive biocatalytic reductions and oxygenations by NADH-dependent oxidoreductases with formate as a cheap, atom-economic terminal reductant. However, despite the clear benefits over other recycling systems, native FDHs remain rather unpopular, mainly due to their intrinsic, low specific activity. While the active site architecture is generally highly conserved across many FDHs from very diverse origins, smaller patterns of dissonance in the active site's vicinity can serve as hotspots for the rat
papers.journal: Chembiochem : a European journal of chemical biology
papers.summary: This study improves the activity and stability of Candida boidinii formate dehydrogenase (FDH) through rational active site engineering, addressing the enzyme's low specific activity that limits its use in cofactor regeneration for biocatalysis. By identifying and modifying key residues near the active site, the authors achieved enhanced enzyme performance, making FDH more practical for industrial applications.

papers.title: Hierarchical Discrete Representations for Coarse-to-Fine Protein Conformation Generation.
papers.abstract: Protein conformation generation remains a fundamental challenge in structural biology and machine learning. Proteins are highly dynamic macromolecules, and their functions are governed not only by static 3D structures but also by their conformational flexibility. Therefore, generating a diverse ensemble of physically plausible structures is crucial for modeling conformational heterogeneity, characterizing intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs), and supporting structure-based drug discovery. However, existing generative models often operate in continuous coordinate space. This approach makes
papers.summary: This paper introduces a hierarchical discrete representation approach for generating protein conformations in a coarse-to-fine manner, addressing the challenge of modeling conformational flexibility beyond static structures. The method aims to improve the generation of diverse, physically plausible protein ensembles, which is important for studying intrinsically disordered proteins and supporting drug discovery.

papers.title: Active ingredients and molecular targets of Tripterygium wilfordii against colorectal cancer: network pharmacology, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations and in vitro evaluation.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is one of the common malignant tumors of the gastrointestinal tract, encompassing both colon cancer and rectal cancer. This study explores the therapeutic potential of T. wilfordii in CRC through network pharmacology, molecular docking, and in vitro experiments.
papers.summary: This study uses network pharmacology, molecular docking, and in vitro experiments to identify active ingredients of Tripterygium wilfordii (a traditional Chinese medicine) and their molecular targets against colorectal cancer. The findings suggest specific compounds and pathways that may underlie its anti-cancer effects, providing a basis for further drug development.

papers.title: Integrated computational and preclinical evaluation of drug repurposing candidates for KRAS-mutant non-small cell lung cancer.
papers.abstract: KRAS mutations, particularly KRAS G12C, pose significant therapeutic challenges in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) due to limited inhibitor efficacy and rapid resistance. Drug repurposing offers a time and cost-effective strategy to identify alternative therapeutic options targeting KRAS-driven signalling. A structure-based drug repurposing approach was employed to screen FDA-approved compounds targeting key regulators to the MAPK signalling pathway and computationally modelled for potential engagement with the KRAS G12C switch-II pocket. Computational analyses including virtual screening,
papers.summary: This study uses a structure-based computational approach to screen FDA-approved drugs for repurposing against KRAS-mutant non-small cell lung cancer, focusing on compounds that may bind the KRAS G12C switch-II pocket. The authors identify promising drug candidates and validate them through preclinical models, offering potential alternative therapeutic options for this challenging cancer subtype.

papers.title: Phlorizin attenuates chronic kidney disease induced bone loss by mitigating sclerostin mediated inhibition of Wnt/β-catenin signaling and ameliorating metabolic alterations.
papers.abstract: CKD-MBD is a metabolic disorder characterized by disrupted mineral metabolism, leading to vascular calcification, renal osteodystrophy, and high fracture risk. Sclerostin, an osteocyte-derived Wnt inhibitor, is a key regulator of both bone loss and vascular calcification. This study explored the role of phlorizin (SGLT1 and SGLT2 inhibitor) on bone loss and metabolic profile in CKD-MBD. Calvarial osteoblasts were treated with phlorizin and evaluated for ALP activity, viability, mineralization, and gene/protein expression. Molecular docking and simulation studies were performed to check phloriz
papers.summary: This study investigates the potential of phlorizin, an SGLT1/2 inhibitor, to treat bone loss associated with chronic kidney disease-mineral and bone disorder (CKD-MBD). The findings suggest that phlorizin attenuates CKD-induced bone loss by mitigating sclerostin-mediated inhibition of Wnt/β-catenin signaling and improving metabolic alterations, as demonstrated through in vitro osteoblast experiments and molecular docking simulations.

papers.title: Frankenia hirsuta-derived biofunctionalized ZnO nanoparticles attenuate inflammation-associated tissue injury: Integrated pharmacological evaluation supported by network pharmacology and molecular docking.
papers.abstract: Inflammation-associated tissue injury is driven by complex interactions among inflammatory mediators, oxidative stress, and apoptosis, creating a need for therapeutic strategies capable of targeting multiple pathological processes. Plant-mediated zinc oxide nanoparticles (ZnO NPs) have attracted increasing interest because of their favorable biocompatibility and pharmacological potential. This study comprehensively evaluated the phytochemical composition, physicochemical characteristics, and anti-inflammatory efficacy of Frankenia hirsuta-derived biofunctionalized ZnO nanoparticles (FH-ZnONPs)
papers.summary: This study demonstrates that zinc oxide nanoparticles synthesized using Frankenia hirsuta plant extract (FH-ZnONPs) exhibit anti-inflammatory properties by reducing tissue injury through modulation of inflammatory mediators, oxidative stress, and apoptosis. The authors integrated experimental pharmacological evaluation with network pharmacology and molecular docking to identify potential molecular targets and mechanisms, supporting the therapeutic potential of these biofunctionalized nanoparticles for inflammation-associated conditions.

papers.title: On Void Formation during the Simulated Tensile Testing of Polymer-Filler Particle Composites.
papers.abstract: We simulate model polymer composites composed of linear polymer strands and spherical, monodisperse filler particles (FP). These molecular dynamics simulations implement a coarse-grained, bead-spring force field, and we vary several formulation parameters to study their influences on material properties. These parameters include FP radius, FP volume fraction, temperature, and the polymer-polymer, FP-FP, and polymer-FP interaction potentials. Uniaxial extension of the simulation cells allows direct comparison of the mechanical reinforcement (or weakening) provided by the FP. We focus on the for
papers.summary: This study uses molecular dynamics simulations to investigate how filler particle size, volume fraction, temperature, and interaction potentials affect void formation and mechanical properties in polymer composites during tensile testing. The findings provide insights into the mechanisms of mechanical reinforcement and failure in these materials.

papers.title: Nitrogen Fixation by MoSn3 and MoSn5 Clusters.
papers.abstract: The Haber-Bosch process (HBP) for the conversion of nitrogen into ammonia is arguably one of the most important chemical reactions in human history because it is the basis for the large-scale production of fertilizers and hence of global food production. Nevertheless, the HBP contributes in a decisive manner to the production of CO2 and other global warming gases, since it is an extremely energy-intensive process. Consequently, the development of alternative conditions to reduce its negative environmental impact is of the highest priority. In this study, we investigate the detailed mechanism o
papers.summary: This study computationally investigates the mechanism of nitrogen fixation by MoSn3 and MoSn5 clusters, proposing them as potential alternatives to the energy-intensive Haber-Bosch process. The findings suggest these clusters may offer a more sustainable route for ammonia production, though the work is primarily theoretical and at an early stage.

papers.title: New structures of human formylglycine-generating enzyme reveal features important for catalysis, disease and structure-based drug design.
papers.abstract: The formylglycine-generating enzyme (FGE) post-translationally modifies the active site of all human sulfatases. Mutations in the SUMF1 gene encoding FGE may lead to catalytically inactive FGE or destabilize the protein. The resulting lack of sulfatase modification causes the rare disease multiple sulfatase deficiency (MSD). Previously, FGE required elastase treatment for crystallization and the structures lacked copper, although FGE is a copper-dependent enzyme. Here, we show that highly active human FGE purified from insect cells natively contains one copper ion and we report six new crystal
papers.summary: This study presents new crystal structures of human formylglycine-generating enzyme (FGE) that natively contain copper, revealing key features for catalysis, disease mutations, and potential drug design. The findings improve understanding of FGE's copper-dependent mechanism and provide a structural basis for developing therapies for multiple sulfatase deficiency.

papers.title: Rational design, synthesis, and antimicrobial evaluation of novel 1,2,3-triazole hybrids: structure-activity relationships, molecular docking, and DFT studies.
papers.abstract: A series of novel 2,4-dichlorophenyl-1,2,3-triazole derivatives and their structural hybrids incorporating chalcone, hydrazone, thio/semicarbazide, carbamate, and pyrazole moieties were rationally designed, synthesized, and characterized. The antimicrobial activity of the synthesized compounds was evaluated against Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria, as well as Candida albicans, revealing clear structure-dependent activity profiles. Among the tested compounds, the parent triazole-acetyl scaffold (compound 3) exhibited the most consistent broad-spectrum activity, with MIC values of 22.5 m
papers.summary: This study reports the rational design and synthesis of novel 1,2,3-triazole hybrids with various structural modifications, evaluating their antimicrobial activity against bacteria and fungi. The parent triazole-acetyl scaffold showed the most consistent broad-spectrum activity, and structure-activity relationships were supported by molecular docking and DFT studies.

papers.title: Integrative computational toxicology and experimental validation unveils ESR1-mediated steroidogenic disruption in triphenyl phosphate-induced female reproductive toxicity.
papers.abstract: Triphenyl phosphate (TPHP), an organophosphorus flame retardant, has emerged as a significant environmental concern due to its persistence and potential health hazards. However, its role in female reproductive toxicity remains poorly understood, necessitating systematic evaluation of its molecular mechanisms. This study integrated network toxicology, transcriptomics, machine learning, adverse outcome pathway (AOP) framework, molecular docking, and in vitro experiments to systematically investigate TPHP-induced reproductive toxicity. Network analysis identified 24 TPHP-infertility shared target
papers.summary: This study combines computational toxicology approaches (network analysis, transcriptomics, machine learning, AOP framework, molecular docking) with in vitro experiments to uncover the molecular mechanisms of triphenyl phosphate (TPHP)-induced female reproductive toxicity. The findings highlight ESR1-mediated steroidogenic disruption as a key pathway, providing a systematic understanding of TPHP's reproductive health risks.

papers.title: Sparsomycin inhibits translation through a conserved mechanism across all domains of life.
papers.abstract: Sparsomycin (SPA) is a broad-spectrum inhibitor of protein synthesis with activity across all three domains of life. Although SPA has long been known to target the ribosomal peptidyl transferase center (PTC), previous structural studies suggested that SPA binds differently to bacterial ribosomes compared to their archaeal and eukaryotic counterparts-an unexpected conclusion given the high evolutionary conservation of the ribosomal catalytic center. Here, we show that SPA inhibits a majority of elongation-competent bacterial ribosomal complexes and present X-ray crystal structures of Thermus th
papers.summary: This study reveals that the antibiotic sparsomycin inhibits translation through a conserved mechanism across all domains of life, contrary to previous suggestions of domain-specific binding. Using X-ray crystallography and biochemical assays, the authors show that sparsomycin binds to the ribosomal peptidyl transferase center in a similar manner in bacteria, archaea, and eukaryotes, and inhibits most elongation-competent bacterial ribosomal complexes. The findings clarify the universal mode of action of this broad-spectrum inhibitor and highlight the evolutionary conservation of the ribosome's catalytic core.

papers.title: Systematic mapping of insertion-tolerant regions enables capsid engineering of an infectious RNA phage.
papers.abstract: RNA phages are attractive platforms for the design of programmable bioparticles, but their development has been constrained by limited knowledge of genomic sites that can tolerate sequence insertion. Here, we combined MuA transposase-mediated in vitro insertion mutagenesis with our established reverse genetics systems to systematically identify insertion-tolerant regions (ITRs) in the RNA phages MS2 and PP7. Screening of 4,555 MS2 and 2,228 PP7 random insertion clones identified 29 and 26 non-redundant ITRs, respectively. We further analyzed and compared these ITRs in the context of RNA genome
papers.summary: This study systematically maps genomic regions in the RNA phages MS2 and PP7 that can tolerate sequence insertions, using transposase-mediated mutagenesis and reverse genetics. The authors identify dozens of insertion-tolerant regions and demonstrate their utility for capsid engineering, providing a valuable resource for designing programmable RNA phage-based bioparticles.

papers.title: A hierarchically organized communication network underlies kinetic allostery in SARS-CoV-2 Mpro.
papers.abstract: The SARS-CoV-2 main protease (Mpro) is an essential viral enzyme whose catalytic activity strictly depends on dimerization and inter-protomer functional communication. While hundreds of symmetrical ligand-free or fully occupied structures are available, the structural and dynamical mechanisms governing asymmetric long-range communication remain elusive, hampering the rational development of non-competitive, allosteric inhibitors. Here, we leverage unconventional, asymmetrical crystal structures captured in a singly occupied, peptide-bound state to uncover the structural baseline of Mpro kineti
papers.summary: This study uses asymmetric crystal structures of SARS-CoV-2 Mpro in a singly occupied state to reveal how dimerization and inter-protomer communication drive kinetic allostery. The findings identify a hierarchically organized communication network that could inform the design of allosteric inhibitors.

papers.title: Broad-Spectrum Multi-Epitope Design Targeting Conserved Hantavirus Glycoproteins (Gn/Gc): Chimeric Antigen Engineering and Structural Mapping.
papers.abstract: Hantaviruses, the etiological agents of hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) and hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS), represent a high-risk zoonotic threat with substantial global health impact. Currently, there is no FDA-approved vaccine. The viral surface glycoprotein (GP) is crucial for host cell entry and is regarded as a key target for vaccine development. However, its variability among hantavirus species limits the effectiveness of conventional vaccine strategies. Epitope-based vaccines offer a promising alternative by enabling the design of broadly protective constructs. In this
papers.summary: This study presents a computational design of a broad-spectrum multi-epitope vaccine targeting conserved regions of hantavirus glycoproteins (Gn/Gc), using chimeric antigen engineering and structural mapping. The approach aims to overcome the challenge of viral glycoprotein variability across hantavirus species, potentially leading to a vaccine effective against multiple strains.

papers.title: Physicochemical, Rheological, and Sensory Characterization of Gluten-Reduced Cookies Enriched with Amaranth and Chickpea Flours.
papers.abstract: The global transition toward plant-based diets necessitates the development of sustainable, nutritionally enriched, and gluten-reduced bakery products. This study evaluated the techno-functional, nutritional, and sensory impacts of substituting wheat flour at levels of 30%, 50%, and 70% with a binary blend of amaranth (Amaranthus caudatus) and chickpea (Cicer arietinum) flours in short-dough cookies. Dough's thermo-mechanical behavior was characterized using the Mixolab Chopin+ protocol and correlated with Texture Profile Analysis (TPA) and consumer acceptability (n = 60) via Principal Compone
papers.summary: This study investigates the effects of substituting wheat flour with amaranth and chickpea flours (30%, 50%, 70%) in gluten-reduced cookies, evaluating dough rheology, texture, and consumer acceptability. Results show that up to 50% substitution maintains acceptable sensory quality while improving nutritional profile, with higher levels negatively impacting dough stability and texture.

papers.title: Effects of L-glutamic acid on wheat starch structure and functionality: multiscale characterization and molecular dynamics simulations.
papers.abstract: L-Glutamic acid (L-Glu) is central to carbon-nitrogen metabolism, yet its ability to improve starch quality by regulating grain metabolism and by directly modulating starch structure remains unclear. In this study, we integrated a field experiment with an in vitro experiment and combined untargeted metabolomics, microscopy, structural characterization, physicochemical and processing property analyses, and molecular dynamics simulations. It was found that under drought, L-Glu spraying reprogrammed the grain metabolome, with pathway enrichment in aminoacyl-tRNA biosynthesis and starch/sucrose me
papers.summary: This study shows that spraying L-glutamic acid on wheat under drought conditions improves starch quality by reprogramming grain metabolism and directly modifying starch structure, as revealed through integrated field and in vitro experiments with multiscale characterization and molecular dynamics simulations. The findings provide new insights into how an amino acid can enhance starch functionality, potentially aiding crop resilience and food processing.

papers.title: From in silico screening to experimental verification: Identification of novel umami peptides from tamarind (Tamarindus indica L.) seed proteins and their validation in enzymatic hydrolysates.
papers.abstract: Umami peptides are key contributors to food flavor enhancement. In this study, novel umami peptides from tamarind seed proteins were identified using an integrated strategy combining in silico screening and experimental validation. A virtual peptide library was screened based on physicochemical properties and bioactivity, yielding six candidates (VSDY, DGIDF, AKNVSDYL, YNDPHC, VPPD, and NDPHCQY). Molecular docking and dynamics simulations revealed stable binding to the umami receptor T1R1/T1R3 via hydrogen bonding and hydrophobic interactions, with binding affinities of -7.9 to -8.8 kcal/mol.
papers.summary: This study identified novel umami peptides from tamarind seed proteins using a combination of in silico screening and experimental validation. Six candidate peptides were found to bind stably to the umami receptor T1R1/T1R3, and their umami taste was confirmed in enzymatic hydrolysates.

papers.title: Experimental, Genomic, and Structural Evidence Supporting Putative PET-Hydrolases in Thermophilic Bacteria Isolated From Hot Springs in Cajamarca, Peru.
papers.abstract: Polyethylene terephthalate (PET) waste represents a major environmental challenge due to limited recycling solutions. Thermophilic bacteria from geothermal environments harbor diverse enzymatic machinery adapted to extreme conditions, offering promising biocatalysts for plastic degradation; however, biological resources from Peru and other South American countries remain scarce. We characterized four bacterial strains isolated from two geothermal sites in Cajamarca, Peru, screened for PET hydrolysis at 50°C. Whole-genome sequencing using hybrid assembly achieved near-complete circular genomes.
papers.summary: This study characterizes four thermophilic bacterial strains from hot springs in Peru, using whole-genome sequencing to identify putative PET-hydrolyzing enzymes. The findings provide new genomic and structural evidence for potential plastic-degrading biocatalysts from under-explored South American geothermal environments.

papers.title: Exploration of Length and Hydrophobicity Requirements for Optimal α-Amylase Secretion in Bacillus subtilis Based on Rational Design.
papers.abstract: The secretory (Sec) pathway is the major pathway of Bacillus subtilis for protein export from the cytoplasm to the extracellular milieu. An amino-terminal signal peptide is required to initiate protein translocation across the cytoplasmic membrane via Sec. Generally, Sec pathway signal peptides of B. subtilis are around 20-30 amino acids long and tend to be relatively hydrophobic compared to signal peptides from other organisms. In view of the importance of signal peptides for high-level secretory protein production, understanding how signal peptide structure and length influence the efficienc
papers.summary: This study systematically investigates how the length and hydrophobicity of signal peptides affect α-amylase secretion in Bacillus subtilis, using rational design to identify optimal parameters. The findings provide practical guidelines for engineering signal peptides to enhance secretory protein production in this industrially important bacterium.

papers.title: A destination-driven framework for nanoparticle-enabled targeted protein degradation.
papers.abstract: Targeted protein degradation (TPD) offers a revolutionary paradigm to eliminate disease-driving proteins. Given the distinct technical requirements and challenges associated with degrading intracellular versus extracellular proteins, we classify existing TPD strategies based on subcellular localization into two categories: intracellular TPD (iTPD), which targets proteins within the cytoplasm and nucleus, and extracellular TPD (eTPD), which focuses on membrane-bound and secreted proteins. This destination-based framework facilitates precise technology selection and rational design by aligning m
papers.summary: This review proposes a framework for classifying targeted protein degradation (TPD) strategies based on the subcellular location of the target protein—intracellular versus extracellular—to guide the rational design of nanoparticle-enabled TPD approaches. It highlights the distinct technical requirements and challenges for each category, aiming to facilitate precise technology selection.

papers.title: Tuning protein corona on nucleic acid nanodrugs for targeted delivery.
papers.abstract: Nanoparticle-based delivery systems hold transformative potential for nucleic acid therapeutics. However, the fate of nucleic acid nanodrugs (NANDs) in vivo differs significantly from that observed in vitro, directly impacting their therapeutic efficacy. Upon introduction into biological fluids, NANDs rapidly adsorb proteins onto their surfaces, forming an assembled adsorption layer known as the protein corona (PC). This PC critically influences the physicochemical properties of NANDs and consequently governs their subsequent biological interactions. This review comprehensively introduces the
papers.summary: This review discusses how the protein corona—a layer of proteins that forms on nucleic acid nanodrugs in biological fluids—affects their behavior and therapeutic efficacy. It highlights strategies to tune the corona for improved targeted delivery, offering insights for designing more effective nanomedicines.

papers.title: Edge-aware GAT-based protein binding sites prediction.
papers.abstract: Accurate identification of protein binding sites is crucial for understanding biomolecular interaction mechanisms and for the rational design of drug targets. Traditional predictive methods often struggle to balance prediction accuracy with computational efficiency when capturing complex spatial conformations. To address this challenge, we propose an Edge-aware Graph Attention Network (Edge-aware GAT) model for the fine-grained prediction of binding sites across various biomolecules, including proteins, DNA/RNA, ions, ligands, and lipids. Our method constructs atom-level graphs and integrates
papers.summary: This paper introduces an Edge-aware Graph Attention Network (GAT) model that improves prediction of protein binding sites for various biomolecules by integrating edge features into atom-level graph representations. The method aims to balance accuracy and computational efficiency, offering a fine-grained approach for identifying interaction sites on proteins.

papers.title: Geometric Deep Learning-Based Drug Design Models for Small-Molecule Drug Discovery.
papers.abstract: Deep neural network (DNN)-based in silico models show great promise in predicting the properties and bioactivities of novel compounds, including small molecules. Among traditional approaches, structure-based drug design (SBDD) remains a fundamental approach for drug discovery using molecular docking, scoring functions, and molecular dynamics simulations. However, these approaches are often constrained by limited flexibility, resolution, and generalizability. Geometric deep learning (GDL) offers a transformative alternative by enabling models to learn directly from non-Euclidean molecular repre
papers.summary: This review discusses how geometric deep learning (GDL) models are transforming small-molecule drug discovery by learning directly from non-Euclidean molecular representations, overcoming limitations of traditional structure-based drug design methods. It highlights GDL's potential to improve property prediction and bioactivity assessment for novel compounds.

papers.title: Identification and Validation of Mannose Metabolism-Related Biomarkers in COPD Through Integrated Bioinformatics and Machine Learning Analysis: A Pilot Study.
papers.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) represents a progressive respiratory disorder marked by sustained airflow restriction and ongoing inflammatory processes. Recently, mannose metabolism has emerged as a significant factor in chronic disease development. This investigation explored how mannose metabolism-related genes (MMRGs) contribute to COPD pathogenesis and evaluated their utility as candidate diagnostic and therapeutic targets.
papers.journal: International journal of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
papers.summary: This pilot study identifies and validates mannose metabolism-related genes as potential biomarkers for COPD using integrated bioinformatics and machine learning approaches. The findings suggest these genes may serve as diagnostic and therapeutic targets, highlighting a novel metabolic angle in COPD pathogenesis.

papers.title: UNKAI: A Protein Functional Identity Prediction Model Based on ESM-C Latent Representations and the Attention Mechanism.
papers.abstract: The rapid advancement of genome sequencing technologies has led to the accumulation of a vast number of protein sequences in public databases. However, a substantial proportion of these proteins remain functionally uncharacterized. Concurrently, the expansion of protein sequence data has enabled the development of protein language models (pLMs). By distilling billions of years of evolutionary history into a latent representational space, these models have acquired an unprecedented capacity to predict both the tertiary structures and functions of proteins. In this study, we developed a deep lea
papers.summary: UNKAI is a new deep learning model that predicts protein function by combining ESM-C language model embeddings with an attention mechanism. It addresses the challenge of functionally uncharacterized proteins in public databases, leveraging evolutionary information captured by protein language models.

papers.title: Molecular docking and dynamics simulation studies uncover the host-pathogen protein-protein interactions in soybean (Glycine max (L.) Merr.) and Groundnut bud necrosis virus: first report.
papers.abstract: Soybean is a widely consumed oilseed crop with economic importance. It is enriched with numerous bioactive compounds that have health-promoting properties. Groundnut bud necrosis virus (GBNV) affects many agriculturally important crops, such as soybean, resulting in crop losses. GBNV is a single-stranded RNA virus from the genus Orthotospovirus and family Bunyaviridae. It is transmitted by insect vectors (thrips) and is further aggravated by secondary transmission from infected plants to others in the same field. There are no commercially available drugs against GBNV; thus, there is a need to
papers.summary: This study uses molecular docking and dynamics simulations to predict host-pathogen protein-protein interactions between soybean and Groundnut bud necrosis virus (GBNV), providing the first reported structural insights into how the virus may hijack soybean proteins. The findings could inform future strategies for developing GBNV-resistant soybean varieties or antiviral interventions.

papers.title: Dynamic structural profiling of PINK1 mutations (T313M and L347P) reveals a vital molecular perturbation namely phospho-Serine 65 ubiquitin recognition point in mitophagy mediated autosomal recessive Parkinson's disease (ARPD).
papers.abstract: Autosomal recessive Parkinson's disease (ARPD) arises from impaired mitophagy due to dysfunction of the PINK1/Parkin pathway, where PINK1-mediated phosphorylation of ubiquitin at Ser65 is essential for pathway activation. However, experimental limitations obscure the effects of disease-associated mutations on intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs) and post-translational modification (PTM) dynamics.
papers.summary: This study uses dynamic structural profiling to investigate how two Parkinson's disease-associated mutations in PINK1 (T313M and L347P) disrupt the protein's function, specifically impairing its ability to recognize phospho-Serine 65 ubiquitin, a critical step in mitophagy. The findings reveal a molecular mechanism linking these mutations to impaired mitophagy and autosomal recessive Parkinson's disease, offering insights that may guide future therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: LNMGAT: a laplacian regularized pseudo-negative mining graph attention network for robust drug-target interaction prediction under multi-scenario cold-start settings.
papers.abstract: Computational drug-target interaction (DTI) prediction provides a scalable alternative to costly and time-consuming experimental screening, but its reliability is limited by the scarcity of experimentally verified negative interactions. In public DTI databases, most unobserved drug-target pairs are unlabeled rather than true non-interactions. Randomly treating these unlabeled pairs as negatives can introduce label noise and reduce model reliability, particularly in cold-start scenarios involving unseen drugs or targets. To address this issue, we propose LNMGAT, a LapRLS-guided reliable pseudo-
papers.summary: This paper introduces LNMGAT, a graph attention network that uses Laplacian regularized pseudo-negative mining to improve drug-target interaction prediction, especially in cold-start scenarios with unseen drugs or targets. The method addresses label noise from unlabeled pairs by generating more reliable pseudo-negatives, enhancing robustness in multi-scenario settings.

papers.title: Bioinformatics-driven design and protective efficacy assessment of a multi-epitope vaccine for Toxoplasma gondii.
papers.abstract: Toxoplasma gondii can cause toxoplasmosis. It is an important type of pathogen within the broad category of emerging and re-emerging zoonoses. As an infectious disease featuring a complex multi-host transmission cycle, it poses an increasingly severe threat to global public health. No licensed vaccines are currently available for pets and humans, and thus a novel high-efficiency vaccine is urgently required.
papers.summary: This study uses bioinformatics to design a multi-epitope vaccine against Toxoplasma gondii and evaluates its protective efficacy, addressing the lack of licensed vaccines for this zoonotic pathogen. The findings support the vaccine candidate's potential for further development.

papers.title: Integrated in vivo and in silico validation of Corchorus olitorius seed-mediated cardioprotection against doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity via network pharmacology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics.
papers.abstract: Corchorus olitorius L., known in Arab countries as molokhia, is a leafy plant rich in many carotenoids, minerals, and vitamins; its seeds are also reported to offer cardioprotective effects. Although the cardioprotective effects of molokhia are ascribed to the presence of cardiac glycoside compounds, the exact action mechanisms remain uninvestigated.
papers.summary: This study validates the cardioprotective effects of Corchorus olitorius (molokhia) seeds against doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity using both in vivo experiments and computational approaches. Network pharmacology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations identified key active compounds and potential molecular targets, providing mechanistic insights into how the seeds protect the heart.

papers.title: Bufothionine inhibits colorectal cancer progression via the STAT3/p53/SLC7A11 signaling axis.
papers.abstract: Bufothionine, a major bioactive component of dried toad skin, has shown anti-tumor potential. However, its efficacy and underlying mechanisms in colorectal cancer (CRC) remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study demonstrates that bufothionine, a compound from dried toad skin, inhibits colorectal cancer progression by modulating the STAT3/p53/SLC7A11 signaling axis, likely through inducing ferroptosis. The findings provide a potential therapeutic mechanism for bufothionine in colorectal cancer treatment.

papers.title: Study on pyrolysis gas generation characteristics of insulating oil under electro-thermal action based on ReaxFF simulation.
papers.abstract: Mineral insulating oil serves as the core insulation and cooling medium of power transformers, and its pyrolysis and gas generation behavior directly determine the safe operation of equipment. Conventional dissolved gas analysis (DGA) only targets small-molecule C1/C2 gases produced in the late pyrolysis stage, which inevitably causes obvious delay in early fault identification. In this work, ReaxFF reactive force field molecular dynamics simulations and physical experiments are jointly adopted to build a multi-component insulating oil molecular model consisting of alkanes, cycloalkanes and ar
papers.summary: This study uses ReaxFF molecular dynamics simulations and experiments to analyze pyrolysis gas generation in insulating oil under electro-thermal stress, revealing early-stage gas products beyond conventional DGA targets. The findings could improve early fault detection in power transformers by identifying additional marker gases.

papers.title: Computational design of immunogenic peptide-ligand conjugates for targeted therapy against Nipah virus infection.
papers.abstract: Nipah virus (NiV) poses a major risk to global public health due to its high infectivity and associated mortality rates. Currently, no licensed vaccines or antiviral medications are available for NiV infection, leaving clinical management limited to supportive care. The viral receptor glycoprotein responsible for binding NiV to host cell receptors (ephrin-B2/B3) represents an ideal therapeutic target. This study proposes a novel peptide-ligand conjugate (PLC) immunotherapeutic approach that exploits pre-existing immune responses in NiV-endemic populations to selectively target and eliminate in
papers.summary: This study computationally designs peptide-ligand conjugates (PLCs) that target the Nipah virus receptor-binding glycoprotein, leveraging pre-existing immune responses in endemic populations for a novel immunotherapeutic approach. The work addresses the urgent need for NiV therapeutics by proposing a targeted strategy that could selectively eliminate infected cells.
